title: Keeping core temperature near 37 °C
caption: The hypothalamus compares blood temperature with the set point. If it is too high, sweating and vasodilation lose heat; if too low, shivering, vasoconstriction and a higher metabolic rate save and make heat. Two opposite responses give finer control.
alt: A flow chart: temperature at the set point needs no response; above it leads to sweating, vasodilation and flattened hairs; below it leads to shivering, vasoconstriction, raised hairs and increased metabolism.
description: The hypothalamus monitors blood temperature and input from skin receptors.
At the set point, about 37 °C, no response is needed.
Too hot: sweating, vasodilation of skin arterioles and hairs lying flat, so more heat is lost.
Too cold: shivering, vasoconstriction, hairs raised and increased metabolism, so heat is kept and made.

q1.q: Is core temperature different from the set point, about 37 °C?

ok.outcome: No response needed: temperature is at the set point

q2.q: Is it above the set point?

hot.outcome: Too hot: sweating, vasodilation of skin arterioles, hairs lie flat

cold.outcome: Too cold: shivering, vasoconstriction, hairs raised, more metabolism
